title: 5.1.19 Lab: Delete the else, watch drift
description: Start from a working WASD movement pattern, delete the two else lines and watch the sprite drift, then restore them and set a speed of your own.

steps.title: Run as-is and confirm movement stops
steps.instructions: Click Run, then click the preview so it gets your keys. Hold a WASD key: the sprite moves. Release it: the sprite stops. That stop is the else-to-zero rule from 5.1.18 at work: each chain ends in an `else` line that sets the velocity back to 0.
hints: Open the moSHion docs drawer on the right and find the Sprite velocity section.

steps.title: Delete the two else lines
steps.instructions: Find the two lines that say `else player.vel.x = 0;` and `else player.vel.y = 0;`. Delete both lines, then click Run.
hints: Look in draw() for the lines starting with `else` that set vel to 0.

steps.title: Tap a key once and watch the sprite drift
steps.instructions: Click the preview to focus it. Tap one WASD key briefly and release. Watch what happens: the sprite keeps moving because vel was never reset.
hints: The sprite drifts because velocity is not automatically reset between frames.

steps.title: Restore the else lines, then pick your speed
steps.instructions: Put both else lines back (`else player.vel.x = 0;` and `else player.vel.y = 0;`) so the sprite stops when no key is held. Then make the speed your own: change the 4s and the -4s to another speed from 2 to 6, as 5.1.17's Try this did. Run it once more: the sprite moves at your speed and still stops the moment you let go. The grader checks that both else lines are back in draw() and that at least one movement line uses a speed other than 4.
hints: Open the moSHion docs drawer on the right and review the velocity section for the correct pattern.
Keep the minus sign on the `a` and `w` lines: `player.vel.x = -3;` moves left and `player.vel.x = 3;` moves right.

requirements.title: Restore else player.vel.x = 0
requirements.description: The draw() function must contain an else branch that sets player.vel.x to 0, so the sprite stops horizontally when no key is held. Help: 5.1.18 (The else-to-zero rule)

requirements.title: Restore else player.vel.y = 0
requirements.description: The draw() function must contain an else branch that sets player.vel.y to 0, so the sprite stops vertically when no key is held. Help: 5.1.18 (The else-to-zero rule)

requirements.title: A speed of your own
requirements.description: At least one movement line in draw() sets player.vel.x or player.vel.y to a speed other than the starter's 4, so the sprite moves at a speed you chose (5.1.17 suggests 2 to 6). Help: 5.1.17 (Movement pattern (if / else if / else))
